title: Qwen4 Max on iac-bench 2026-11

## Summary


Qwen4 Max is new in 2026-11. It ranks 14th of 24 with an overall composite of 78.9 and a 95% rank interval of 11–16. It is not ordered against Gemini 4 Carbon just above it (win probability 0.61) or Gemini 4 Hydrogen just below it (0.72). It finishes ahead of Gemini 4 Neon in 11% of bootstrap resamples and ahead of Kimi K3.1 Pro in 4%, and ahead of GPT-6 Luna and GLM-5.3 in 96%.


All 18 attempts planned. Two carry a security finding: G003 e2 leaves basic-auth publishing on (G003` H2` ), and G004 e1 does not enforce encrypted connections on its secondary cluster (G004` H3` ). All three Aurora global database attempts (G004) have Secrets Manager manage the master password on the primary cluster, a known apply failure, so their composites are halved (median 40.0, 18th). Its strongest fixtures are App Service (G003, 91.3, eighth) and S3 (G001, 83.9, twelfth); Cloud SQL (G002, 81.7) is 19th. All 18 attempts cost $2.16.


Its distinguishing weakness is documentation that contradicts the code. The judge gave *Documentation* 0 in 27 of 54 readings, tied with Gemini 3.8 Flash for the fifth-highest count in the field.


## Changes since the 2026-10 report


Qwen4 Max was not part of the 2026-10 release; this is its first report.

## Strengths


- **S3 with lifecycle rules.** Every S3 attempt offers transition or expiration rules and noncurrent-version handling (G001` H6` ,` H7` kept in 3/3), which GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-6.2 Astra lack in all of theirs. G001 e1 scores 92.9, losing only access logging and half the tagging item.
- **Broad G004 operational coverage.** Every attempt creates a customer-managed KMS key in each region, keeps at least 14 days of backups at defaults (35 in two attempts), and enables Performance Insights and enhanced monitoring (E3, E4, 3/3). G004 e1 also loads pgaudit and logs connections (E1, E2).
- **App Service close to complete.** Every attempt sets the container port and pulls images with a managed identity (E2, E4, 3/3); two have autoscale rules (E1) and one uses Key Vault references (E5). Rubric median 0.926.
- **Storage account names made unique and valid** (E4, 3/3), with portal access defaulting to Entra ID and local users off (E2, E8, 3/3).
- **Outputs.** The judge gave *Outputs* 2 in all 54 readings.


## Weaknesses


- **Secrets Manager on a global member cluster (G004, 3/3).** Every attempt sets` manage_master_user_password = true` on the primary cluster, which Aurora rejects for global databases (F1), so each composite is multiplied by 0.5.
- **An unprotected DR cluster in G004 e1.** The secondary cluster names no parameter group, so` rds.force_ssl` is not set there (G004` H3` , a mandatory failure). A comment in the same file says cluster parameters are inherited from the primary (excerpt below); the judge called that comment inaccurate ( *Documentation* 0 in all three readings).
- **Documentation that contradicts the code.** Examples, each 0 in at least one judge reading:


- Cloud SQL (3/3): the` tier` description suggests` db-perf-optimized-N-2` , an Enterprise Plus tier, while every attempt hardcodes` edition = "ENTERPRISE"` ;
- S3 e2: the README's logs example sets` expiration_days = 30` with the default transition of 90 days, which the module's own precondition rejects;
- GKE: a wrong Workload Identity member format (e1) and a wrong description of authorized networks (e3);
- storage account e3: a claim that App Service passes the` AzureServices` bypass.


- **Large GKE interfaces:** 19–23 inputs against a budget that reaches zero at 21 (G005` A5` , 3/3). Two attempts default` master_ipv4_cidr_block` to a fixed` 172.16.0.0/28` , so a second cluster in the same VPC fails to create (G005` H16` ).
- **Cloud SQL gaps (3/3).** No` deletion_policy` (G002` H11` ), backups and point-in-time recovery always on (G002` H4` /` H5` at 0.75), no maintenance-window input (G002` A4` ), the region fed to the instance rather than the provider (G002` H9` at 0.5), and no` cloudsql.instanceUser` grant, so the IAM users it creates cannot log in (E6, 0/3). G002 e1 also hardcodes deletion protection with no opt-out (G002` H3` ).
- **Basic auth left on in G003 e2.** Neither publishing flag is set on the app or the slot; the other two attempts disable both on both.
- **No blob access logs or lifecycle policy on the storage account** (G006` H7` ,` H9` , 3/3).
- **Provider constraints that admit a new major** in 7 of 18 attempts (` B1` ), including the unbounded` >= 5.0` and` >= 5.40.0` .


## Characteristic patterns


- **Inputs added for specialists the brief does not describe.** The judge marked *Interface design* 1 in 29 of 54 readings, citing knobs such as` abort_multipart_upload_days` on S3,` performance_insights_retention_period` and` kms_deletion_window_in_days` on G004, and` min_master_version` and` enable_intranode_visibility` on GKE.
- **Inline security-group rules on G004.** All three attempts declare` ingress` inline on` aws_security_group` ( *Inline Resource Configuration* 0 in 8 of 9 G004 readings, 1 in the ninth).
- **Validation that rejects valid values,** such as a Performance Insights retention check that rejects 731 days (G004 e3), a maintenance start time limited to whole hours (G005 e3) and a` location` regex that rejects "West Europe" (G006 e1).
- **Long, commented files.** Median output is 14,631 tokens per attempt, and the G004 modules run to 624–725 source lines.


## Representative excerpt


` G004/qwen4-max-e1/secondary.tf` lines 7–12


```text
# Notes on global-database semantics:
#   * credentials, database name and cluster parameters are inherited from
#     the primary - they are intentionally NOT set here
#   * a region-local CMK is required for the encrypted secondary storage
#   * the cluster can only be created once the primary has an instance
#     (hence the explicit depends_on)


```


` G004/qwen4-max-e1/secondary.tf` lines 24–32


```text
port = var.port


storage_encrypted = true
kms_key_id        = aws_kms_key.secondary.arn


db_subnet_group_name   = aws_db_subnet_group.secondary.name
vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.secondary.id]


iam_database_authentication_enabled = true


```


The secondary cluster of G004 e1 sets no parameter group, on the strength of a comment saying cluster parameters are inherited from the primary. Without one, rds.force_ssl is not enforced on the cluster that becomes the writer after a failover (G004 H3, a mandatory failure); the judge scored the comment as incorrect documentation.
